Animation

class pygeox.animate.AnimateNamespace(scene)[source]

Bases: object

Namespace to manage animation parameters and generate animations by varying parameters within a geometric scene.

Provides functionality to add animation parameters, run animations by solving constraints at discrete parameter values, and export animations as GIFs.

add_parameter(name, total_time=1)[source]

Add a new symbolic animation parameter to the scene.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – The name of the animation parameter.

  • total_time (int | float | Expr | Symbol)

Returns:

The sympy.Symbol representing the animation parameter.

eval_piecewise_at_zero(expr, anim_syms)[source]

If expr contains Piecewise, pick the first branch whose condition is: - literally True, or - an And(…, alpha >= 0, …) (ignoring other bounds), or - becomes True after substituting alpha -> 0. Otherwise (no Piecewise), return expr unchanged.

point_sweep_arc(point, arc, counterclockwise=True, total_time=2, speed=None)[source]

Animate a point moving along an arc by directly constraining its x and y coordinates. Point moves from arc.start_point to arc.end_point over the arc length.

Parameters:

  • point (Point)

  • arc (MinorArc | MajorArc)

  • counterclockwise (bool)

  • total_time (int | float | Expr | Symbol | None)

  • speed (int | float | Expr | Symbol | None)

point_sweep_circle(point, circle, counterclockwise=True, total_time=2, speed=None)[source]

Animate a point moving around a circle by directly constraining its x and y coordinates. Point starts at the top of the circle and moves counterclockwise by default.

Parameters:

point_sweep_polyline(point, path_points, total_time=5, speed=None)[source]

Animates a point moving smoothly along a polyline defined by a sequence of points.

A single parameter time_param in [0, 1] controls the point’s position. As time_param increases from 0 to 1, the point traverses each segment of the polyline in proportion to segment length. A single sympy.Piecewise constraint ensures that the point’s coordinates match the appropriate interpolated position along the active segment.

Parameters:

  • point (Point) – The Point object to animate.

  • path_points (List[Point]) – Ordered list of points defining the polyline path.

  • total_time (int | float | Expr | Symbol | None)

  • speed (List[int | float | Expr | Symbol] | None)

run(moving_points, frames=20, opt_method='dual_annealing', distance_penalty=1, min_dist=None, run_type='independent')[source]

Generate a sequence of solved scenes by interpolating animation parameters from 0 to 1, effectively creating frames of the animation.

Points not listed in moving_points are fixed to their initial positions.

Parameters:

  • moving_points (List[Point]) – A list of Point objects that are allowed to move during animation. Points not in this list will remain fixed.

  • frames (int) – The number of frames to generate in the animation.

  • opt_method (str) – The numerical solver method to use for constraint solving. Refer to scipy.optimize.minimize for available options.

  • distance_penalty (float | None) – The penalty weight to avoid degenerate cases related to area and point distances. This is used in the first frame and as a penalty constraint. It is removed from the moving points.

  • min_dist (float | None) – The minimum allowed distance between points. This is only used for the first frame.

  • run_type (Literal['independent', 'together'])

Raises:

ValueError – If no animation parameters are defined in the scene.
